new_candidates.body:
Hi organizers, thanks for running this challenge.

We are a team from Southeast University in mainland China. The Official Terms (official-2026-08), Section 2, list the People's Republic of China among excluded jurisdictions, and the Challenge Page notes that "some teams may be ineligible for prizes". Could you please clarify:

1. If a team based in mainland China finishes first in a track, will it be officially recognized as the track winner, for example listed as the winner in the final results announcement, given a winner certificate, and invited to present its method, even if the hardware prize cannot be delivered?
2. After the final submission, can a team update its organization/affiliation or add an additional affiliation (as discussed in #209), and would that change be reflected on the final leaderboard and in the results announcement?

Thank you!
new_candidates.title: Clarification on prize eligibility for teams based in mainland China

new_candidates.body:
## Description

Expose per-topic dropped-message counts during rosbag2 recording so callers can
monitor data loss in real time without waiting for a bag split or close.

Our recorder counts its message rate at the subscription, before the cache, so a
recorder discarding a third of its data reports exactly the same numbers as a
healthy one. The first indication anything was lost is a log line at close, by
which point the data is gone.

Same on [`rolling`](https://github.com/ros2/rosbag2/blob/rolling/rosbag2_cpp/include/rosbag2_cpp/cache/message_cache.hpp#L121-L123),
so this isn't already addressed in a later release.

Alternatively, a callback triggered when messages are dropped would also solve
this problem.

**Version:** rosbag2 `0.26.11` (Jazzy)

## Related Issues

None known.

## Completion Criteria

- [ ] Dropped-message counts are queryable per topic during recording
- [ ] Counts match those reported by `log_dropped()` at close
- [ ] Reading counts is thread-safe during concurrent recording
- [ ] Behaviour is defined for disabled caching and snapshot mode
- [ ] The feature is documented alongside the cache options

## Implementation Notes / Suggestions

Consider adding a dropped-count accessor to `MessageCacheInterface` and exposing
it through the writer.

The count already exists as `MessageCache::messages_dropped_per_topic_`, but it
is `protected` and there is no route to it from outside. Links are to `0.26.11`:

| what | where |
|---|---|
| the count | [`message_cache.hpp#L114-L116`](https://github.com/ros2/rosbag2/blob/0.26.11/rosbag2_cpp/include/rosbag2_cpp/cache/message_cache.hpp#L114-L116) |
| incremented here | [`message_cache.cpp#L56-L57`](https://github.com/ros2/rosbag2/blob/0.26.11/rosbag2_cpp/src/rosbag2_cpp/cache/message_cache.cpp#L56-L57) |
| only exposed via `log_dropped()` | [`message_cache_interface.hpp#L38-L75`](https://github.com/ros2/rosbag2/blob/0.26.11/rosbag2_cpp/include/rosbag2_cpp/cache/message_cache_interface.hpp#L38-L75) |
| writer holds it `protected` | [`sequential_writer.hpp#L153`](https://github.com/ros2/rosbag2/blob/0.26.11/rosbag2_cpp/include/rosbag2_cpp/writers/sequential_writer.hpp#L153) |

```cpp
// what we'd want on MessageCacheInterface
virtual std::unordered_map<std::string, uint32_t> get_dropped_counts() const;
```

> [!NOTE]
> The map is mutated without a lock at
> [`message_cache.cpp#L56-L57`](https://github.com/ros2/rosbag2/blob/0.26.11/rosbag2_cpp/src/rosbag2_cpp/cache/message_cache.cpp#L56-L57).
> That's safe today because `push` only runs under `Writer::writer_mutex_`, but
> a public getter introduces readers outside that mutex.

## Testing Notes / Suggestions

- Verify counts are readable and increase **during** recording, not only at close
- Verify per-topic counts match `log_dropped()` at close
- Test disabled caching (`max_cache_size == 0`) and snapshot mode
- Test concurrent reads during recording, ideally under TSan
new_candidates.title: Expose the per-topic dropped-message count from MessageCache at runtime
